_comment: Curated historical space-weather events for the space-weather.html timeline scrubber. Read-only. Append new events to the array; the page picks them up on next load with no code change. Sources are documented per event (NOAA SWPC G/R lists, Kyoto WDC, peer-reviewed papers) — the same record base HeliochroniCles compiles. Do not add uncertain/apocryphal events.

events.label: Carrington Event
events.summary: The most intense geomagnetic storm in recorded history. Telegraph systems worldwide failed; aurorae were seen from the Caribbean.

events.label: Quebec Blackout 1989
events.summary: A severe geomagnetic storm collapsed the Hydro-Quebec grid in 92 seconds, leaving six million people without power for ~9 hours. The benchmark grid-impact event.

events.label: Bastille Day 2000
events.summary: An X5.7 flare on 14 July 2000 launched a fast Earth-directed halo CME, producing a G5 storm and a strong solar proton event. A classic flare-CME-storm chain.

events.label: Halloween Storms 2003
events.summary: A series of X-class flares including X17.2 (Oct 28) and the saturation-class X28+ (Nov 4). SOHO LASCO C2/C3 were saturated; airline routes were diverted.

events.label: St. Patrick's Day 2015
events.summary: The largest geomagnetic storm of solar cycle 24, driven by a CME compounded by a corotating high-speed stream. Widely studied for its two-step main phase.

events.label: Starlink Loss Event
events.summary: A merely G1 storm raised thermospheric density enough to deorbit 38 of 49 newly launched Starlink satellites; NRLMSIS underpredicted density by ~30%. The anchor case for physics-first vs ML drag modelling.

events.label: Gannon Storm
events.summary: The first G5 storm since 2003, from a sequence of CMEs out of AR 13664. Low-latitude aurorae worldwide; many operators reported drag-induced orbit decay and anomalies.

events.label: AR 3664 X8.7 Flare
events.summary: An X8.7 flare from AR 13664 on 14 May 2024 — the largest flare of solar cycle 25 at the time, immediately following the Gannon storm.

events.label: AR 3842 X9.0 Flare
events.summary: An X9.0 flare from AR 13842 on 3 October 2024, the strongest of solar cycle 25 to date. Used as a validation case for the Parkers Physics MHD flare simulation.

events.label: October 2024 G4 Storm
events.summary: A severe G4 storm on 10-11 October 2024 from an AR 13848 halo CME, again producing widespread mid-latitude aurorae.

events.label: AR 3590 X6.3 Flare
events.summary: An X6.3 flare from AR 13590 on 22 February 2024, the largest of cycle 25 until the May 2024 sequence surpassed it.

events.label: New Year's Eve 2023 X5.0
events.summary: An X5.0 flare from AR 13536 on 31 December 2023 — the largest flare since the September 2017 X8.2 at the time.

events.label: September 2017 Storm
events.summary: AR 12673 produced an X9.3 (6 Sep) and an X8.2 limb flare (10 Sep) with a strong proton event, driving a G4 storm during the rising activity gap of cycle 24.
